rule: **Python**: module-qualified IDs from the package structure (directories with `__init__.py`): `pkg.mod.f`, `pkg.mod.C#m`, `pkg.mod.C#<init>`, nested functions `pkg.mod.f.inner` / `pkg.mod.C#m.inner`; module-level code's caller is the module name, class-body code's caller is `pkg.mod.C`. Imports (relative, aliased, star, re-exported via `__init__.py`) resolve to the defining module. Builtins are `builtins.len` (medium). **C1 Symbol identity.** Every definition has exactly one ID. Every reference to it uses that ID: a call in the defining file, through an import, a re-export, an alias or a `require` binding. A definition that edges reach is listed in `nodes`, including body-less member declarations of scanned types (interface/trait/protocol methods) and module-level bindings that hold a function. A high edge's callee is always in `nodes`. **C2 Resolution consistency.** The same written reference in the same scope resolves the same way wherever it occurs. Resolution does not depend on file order, the scan root, or which other files are present, except through the definitions those files supply. An ID is never invented: a medium or high callee that names a member of a scanned module or type (`mod.T#f`, `mod.f`) is defined there, or is inherited from a base outside the scan.
notes: C1: `slugify` is referenced from its own file (util.py:6) and from page.py through a relative import (10), a relative module alias `u.slugify` (11), an aliased absolute import (12), a re-export via shop/__init__.py (13) and a fully qualified module path (15); every reference is `shop.util.slugify`. `title_slug` arrives through a star import (14) and is `shop.util.title_slug`. Import statements, including the re-export in __init__.py, are not calls (C3). `text` is a parameter of unknown type -> `text.lower` / `text.title`, low.
